sources.full: Trouble at Grog's — Hall Qualification Conversion

contents.name: Chapter 3: Return to the Happy Orc
Appendix B: Clues and Failure Modes

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Three-hour Hall of Heroes qualification one-shot for four or five 3rd-level PCs.
Run three substantive investigation beats unless the players solve the case sooner. Treat the investigation as a situation, not a prescribed sequence.
Clues fail forward. Never hide an essential conclusion behind one roll.
Assume the PCs reach the finale with most major resources and are willing to spend every spell slot, Rage, Action Surge, healing resource, consumable, and subclass resource they have.
The final battle is deliberately hard. One or more PCs can hit 0 hit points, but enemies do not repeatedly attack unconscious PCs while conscious threats remain.
Named cast only: Grog, Yuri Kinnon, Sid Barrow, Grunt, Jim Ramsey, Ellie Felan. Do not reintroduce removed named NPCs.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Grog is an orc adventurer-turned-innkeeper whose Happy Orc tavern has become one of Dagger Rock's most popular establishments. It is cheap, generous, welcoming, and successful.
Yuri Kinnon owns the competing Dagger Rock Tavern. His motive is simple: Grog's place is more successful than his, and Yuri wants Grog ruined.

Yuri manufactures a crime wave around Grog. Grunt burns a stable. Jim Ramsey falsely claims he saw an orc fleeing the fire. Ellie Felan steals property and plants it in the underground cellar beneath the Happy Orc so a later search appears to prove Grog is behind the thefts.
Sid Barrow is the honest captain of the guard and Grog's friend. Sid corroborates the PCs' work rather than solving the mystery for them.

entries.name: The Conspiracy

entries.caption: Frame-Up Chain
rows: Commits the stable arson and provides muscle.
Physical evidence, surveillance, capture, or confession.
Creates the accusation by falsely claiming an orc fled the stable.
Contradictions, sightline/timeline evidence, pressure, magic, or surveillance.
Creates the physical case by stealing and planting property in the Happy Orc's underground cellar.
Catch her moving goods; match items to Sid's inventory; expose the cellar cache.
Two independent links to Yuri, or one strong Yuri link plus decisive physical evidence.

entries: Mental model: Grunt creates the crime; Jim creates the lie; Ellie creates the evidence; Yuri coordinates.
The burned stable is not Grog's property and has no legitimate connection to him.

entries.caption: Real-Time Clock
rows: Character introductions and arrival in Dagger Rock.
Enter the Happy Orc, meet Grog, understand the problem.
Three investigation beats, about 10–15 minutes each.
Ask the players what they think is happening and what they do next.
Corroboration, pursuit, accusation, or Yuri's reaction.
Return to the Happy Orc, evacuation, enemy placement, initiative.
Secure cellar evidence; Sid clears Grog.

entries.caption: Six Named NPCs
rows: Huge-looking, extremely friendly owner; innocent client.
Respectable rival tavern owner; sole mastermind; finale boss.
Honest guard captain; verifies facts and handles the legal outcome.
Human mercenary; stable arsonist and muscle.
Former thief posing as a harmless drunk; false witness and rumor-spreader.
Elf thief/spellcaster; steals and plants evidence; tries to reach the cellar in the finale.

entries.name: Physical Map — Locked Build
entries: Use the embedded Happy Orc Social Setup as the canonical physical build. The generated picture is a placement guide; at the table use the actual L-shaped AF634A bar rather than the U-shaped bar shown by the generator.
The build sits on a 22 × 26 one-inch battle mat and uses only confirmed STAHLHAMMERS wall pieces and AF634A tavern furniture.

entries.caption: Main-Floor Layout
rows: Northwest/back-left. Compact. Clear access from the common room.
Northeast/back-right. Clear door from the common room and rear exit in its north wall.
Not a main-floor room. Draw the cellar entrance in the storage room. The planted evidence is downstairs.
West side. Use the real L-shaped bar. Five stools are out during the social scene.
Largest public zone, center and south-center. Exactly two round tables and eight dining chairs, four per table.
East wall: small fireplace, the single white animal-hide rug, and two lounge chairs.
Small floor-level southeast performance corner using the two crossbar stands and minimal confirmed scatter. No stage.
Centered on the south wall, using a door-wall module.
North wall of the storage room, using a door-wall module.

entries: No windows, plants, shrubs, extra rugs, stage, pillars, extra furniture, or unconfirmed terrain belong in this build.

entries.name: Opening Read-Aloud

entries: The Happy Orc is easy to find: laughter, clattering mugs, and the smell of hot food spill into the street before you reach the door. Inside, a broad orc behind the bar looks like he could throw a horse through a window. Instead, he grins, waves you in, and calls, "Find a seat. If you leave hungry, that's my fault."
Play the room as visibly successful: both dining tables in use, bar stools occupied, a tight fireplace nook, and a small performance corner. People like being here.

entries.name: Grog
entries: Grog is physically imposing and emotionally disarming. He laughs easily, remembers orders, gives away a little too much food, and treats strangers as future regulars.
He does not know who is framing him. He has noticed only the pattern: more crimes, more anti-orc rumors, and more claims that the Happy Orc is connected.
He hires outsiders because local loyalties and gossip are already tangled. He wants the truth, not revenge.
"Somebody wants people scared of this place. I can punch a man. Harder problem is punching a rumor."

entries.name: The Job
entries: Grog tells the PCs that a stable recently burned and a witness claims an orc ran from the scene. Other stolen goods have also been blamed on his patrons.
He asks the PCs to find out who is doing it and why. Establish payment only if needed; Grog pays after the case is resolved.
If they investigate Grog himself, let them. They find ordinary tavern flaws, not organized-crime evidence.

entries.caption: Opening Leads
rows: The fire was deliberate; Jim's story does not fit the scene; physical trail toward Grunt.
The orc eyewitness story is rehearsed and false; Yuri-linked payment/contact is possible.
Verified timeline, stolen-property inventory, and contradictions between rumor and evidence.
Arsonist/muscle; direct employer link to Yuri if pressured or captured.
The planted cache is underground; Ellie is the person moving evidence.

entries.name: Running the Investigation
entries: Run three substantive beats unless the players solve the case sooner. A beat costs about 10–15 minutes.
Use DC 12 for cooperative/easy pressure, DC 14 for guarded people or useful scene analysis, and DC 16 for frightened liars or subtle evidence. If the method logically works, do not call for a roll.
Failure should cost time, create suspicion, produce partial information, or alert Yuri. Failure never deletes the only path forward.
Do not require the PCs to visit every lead. Move important facts to another logical source when the table skips a location.

entries.name: Stable Fire

entries: The stable smells of wet ash and scorched hay. One side of the structure is blackened almost to the ground, but the damage is strangely concentrated near the rear wall. Townsfolk keep repeating the same detail: somebody saw an orc running away.
The stable belongs to an unnamed local owner and has no connection to Grog.

entries.caption: Stable Clues
rows: The fire started low at the rear wall in more than one place. Deliberate arson.
Inspect ground — DC 14 Investigation or Survival
Heavy boot tracks approach the rear, pause near ignition points, then leave by the alley. Can match Grunt's boots.
Check Jim's claimed viewpoint — no roll once tested
The stable corner blocks the route Jim claims he watched. He cannot reliably identify an orc from there.
Let it work according to the ability; useful information points toward a broad human smelling of smoke/oil, not an orc.
Coarse dark cloth and lamp-oil residue support deliberate close-range ignition; cloth can match Grunt.

entries.name: Jim Ramsey

entries: Jim Ramsey has the practiced collapse of a man who wants everyone to underestimate him: rumpled coat, watery eyes, cup always in hand. His story is ready before the question is finished. "Big orc. Ran from the fire. Saw him clear as day."
Jim is a former thief working for Yuri. His drunk act is partly performance.

entries.caption: Cracking Jim
rows: Compare his sightline to the stable
He starts changing where he says he stood.
His drunkenness slips whenever exact times, Grunt, or Yuri are mentioned.
He admits he was paid to repeat the orc story. If the party already has a Yuri link, he cracks fully.
He makes a Yuri-linked contact or collects money from one of Yuri's people.

entries.name: Grunt
entries: Grunt is a broad, blunt mercenary who prefers intimidation to conversation. He committed the arson for money.
He may tail or threaten the PCs before fighting. If captured or cornered, he identifies Yuri as the employer for the arson/intimidation work.
If neutralized here, he is absent from the finale and is not replaced.

entries.name: Ellie Felan
entries: Ellie is Yuri's theft/evidence specialist and only named lieutenant. She steals property and plants it in the cellar beneath the Happy Orc.
She uses disguise, timing, concealment, and escape magic rather than standing in a fair fight.
Catching her with stolen goods or matching a cache to Sid's inventory can become decisive evidence. If exposed, she tries to move or destroy evidence and warns Yuri if able.

entries.name: Sid Barrow
entries: Sid has a stolen-property inventory and notes separating verified facts from rumors. He corroborates; he does not announce the solution.
If the PCs are stuck, he can identify a stolen item as real and show that Jim's timeline conflicts with verified facts.

entries.name: Yuri Kinnon
entries: Yuri is composed in public. Routine questions make him appear cooperative while he alerts his people. Direct accusation without proof accelerates the endgame.
The finale triggers when player success threatens the scheme, not because a timer expires.

entries.caption: Evidence
rows: Sid treats Yuri as a formal suspect.
Yuri's attack on the Happy Orc

entries.name: 1:15 Decision Checkpoint
entries: At about 1:15, ask the players: "What do you think is happening, and what are you doing next?"
If they have a viable route to Yuri, follow it. If not, use Sid to corroborate one fact they already earned and point them toward the strongest remaining lead.

entries.name: Evacuating the Tavern
entries: Once the PCs warn Grog, he evacuates the Happy Orc. Grog, staff, patrons, and civilians are outside before initiative.
Sid is outside handling law/order and perimeter. Neither Grog nor Sid contributes allied DPR.

During evacuation, some dining chairs are pulled toward walls, bar stools are tucked tighter to the bar, and loose tiny tabletop clutter is removed. The two round tables and all major terrain stay in place.

entries.name: Combat Map — Locked Build
entries: Use the embedded Happy Orc Combat Setup as the canonical finale placement. It is the same tavern build as the Social Setup.
The generated image leaves most furniture in place; at the table manually pull some chairs toward the perimeter and tuck stools tighter to the bar to create the intended movement lanes.
Use the actual L-shaped bar rather than the U-shaped version shown by the generator.
The evidence is not upstairs. It is below in the underground cellar, accessed from the storage room.

entries.name: Finale Trigger
entries: Yuri attacks only after the PCs' success threatens the frame-up. His goal is to destroy, move, or secure the planted evidence and break the case before Sid can act.
Do not trigger this merely because the clock reached a certain minute; the clock tells you when to accelerate consequences.

entries.caption: Starting Positions
rows: Just inside the front entrance, centered.
Farther right/rear; use only for a 5-PC party.
Near the storage-room doorway and cellar route.
If still active, in or immediately outside storage near the rear exit.

entries.name: Enemy Tactics
entries: Yuri presses dangerous PCs, uses allies to enable Dirty Fighting, and uses Parry against the attack most likely to hurt him. Below half hit points he becomes more aggressive.
Ellie uses control, concealment, and mobility to protect the cellar route, then tries to reach the evidence if the fight allows it.
Grunt blocks movement and pressures isolated targets. Hired bandits spread out enough to avoid one easy area spell.
Yuri does not flee or surrender simply because he is losing. At 0 hit points he dies unless the players deliberately take him alive with a legal nonlethal melee attack.
Ellie, Grunt, and hired muscle may flee or surrender when the fight is clearly lost.

entries.name: Cellar Objective
entries: Ellie's priority is the underground planted cache. If she reaches the cellar entrance and can spend an action unopposed, she begins moving or damaging evidence rather than making a damage attack.
Do not erase all evidence on a single action. The PCs should have a chance to interrupt her, recover surviving items, or rely on testimony already earned.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: If Yuri falls and enough evidence survives, Sid clears Grog and arrests surviving conspirators.
If Ellie escapes with some evidence, prior testimony plus Yuri's public violence can still clear Grog if the PCs built a credible case.
End at the Happy Orc. Do not add a council hearing unless the players specifically seek one.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: Primary reward: Grog's name is cleared and the Happy Orc survives.
Grog pays any fee established at the opening; otherwise use the Hall's normal one-shot convention.
Recovered stolen property belongs to its owners. Grog offers food, drink, lodging, and permanent welcome.

entries.name: Grog
entries: Appearance: very large orc, broad shoulders, work-worn tavern clothes, heavy apron, hands marked by old adventuring scars.
Voice: booming, friendly, quick laugh; speaks plainly and assumes people are worth welcoming until they prove otherwise.
Motivation: protect his tavern, patrons, and reputation without becoming the violent stereotype Yuri wants the town to fear.
Knows: the pattern of rumors and accusations; not the mastermind.
Cracks: he does not need to crack—he answers direct questions unless doing so would expose a patron's private business.
Sample: "Eat first. Accuse me after. Nobody thinks well hungry."

entries.name: Yuri Kinnon
entries: Appearance: carefully dressed human proprietor, neat hair, restrained jewelry, clean hands, controlled posture.
Voice: smooth, courteous, slightly too measured; rarely raises his voice until the finale.
Motivation: ruin the rival tavern that eclipsed his own success and preserve his respectable public image.
Knows: the entire plan and every operative's role.
Lies: frames every connection as coincidence, concern for public safety, or somebody else's initiative.
Cracks: hard evidence plus a threatened loss of control; when cornered, courtesy turns cold and personal.
Sample: "You are mistaking a popular story for proof."

entries.name: Sid Barrow
entries: Appearance: sturdy human guard captain in practical, maintained armor; weathered face; no ceremonial fuss.
Voice: low, precise, patient. He separates what he knows from what he suspects.
Motivation: enforce the law without clearing Grog merely because they are friends.
Knows: verified crime reports, stolen-property inventory, witness times, and what evidence is legally useful.
Cracks: not applicable; he cooperates when the PCs bring something concrete.
Sample: "Tell me what you can prove. Then tell me what you think. Keep those two piles separate."

entries.name: Grunt
entries: Appearance: broad human mercenary, coarse dark clothes, battered boots, smoke/oil smell that can connect him to the stable.
Voice: short sentences, impatient, contemptuous of complicated plans.
Motivation: get paid, avoid jail, avoid dying for Yuri.
Knows: Yuri hired him for arson/intimidation and Jim is part of the story.
Lies: claims he was drinking, working, or nowhere near the stable.
Cracks: capture, convincing physical evidence, or realizing Yuri will not protect him.
Sample: "I lit a fire. I didn't build the whole damn scheme."

entries.name: Jim Ramsey
entries: Appearance: rumpled older human, stained coat, watery eyes, cup in hand; looks less alert than he really is.
Voice: slurred when performing, suddenly crisp when surprised.
Motivation: get paid while being dismissed as a harmless drunk.
Knows: he was paid to tell the false orc story and knows how his payment reaches Yuri.
Lies: repeats the same eyewitness story too cleanly.
Cracks: sightline contradiction, exact timeline questions, or sustained pressure.
Sample: "Saw him clear as day. Big orc. You calling me blind?"

entries.name: Ellie Felan
entries: Appearance: lean elf in practical dark travel clothes with a compact satchel; dresses to disappear into a crowd rather than look theatrical.
Voice: quiet, economical, dry; does not waste words when a route to escape exists.
Motivation: protect Yuri's operation and keep the planted evidence usable—or destroy it if exposure is inevitable.
Knows: where stolen items came from, what is already in the cellar, and Yuri's timetable.
Lies: claims she is a courier, patron, or hired hand depending on the scene.
Cracks: caught physically moving stolen goods with no plausible explanation; otherwise she prefers escape to confession.
Sample: "You can argue about what it means after you prove where it came from."

data.name: Appendix B: Clues and Failure Modes

entries.caption: Redundant Clues
rows: Deliberate fire; Jim's false story; planted property.
Physical evidence; tracks; magic; surveillance; confession.
Stolen-goods match; surveillance; caught possession; cellar route.
Grunt employer link; Jim payment/contact; Ellie connection; Yuri's reactions.

entries.name: Portable Clues
entries: If the PCs skip a scene, move facts rather than forcing sightseeing. A payment clue can be on Jim, Grunt, or Ellie. Sid can validate ownership of recovered goods. The stable's sightline contradiction remains available even if examined later.

entries.name: Unexpected Approaches
entries: Let Zone of Truth, Detect Thoughts, Speak with Animals, surveillance, capture, disguise, and early cellar discovery work normally.
Successful magic or clever play can shorten the mystery; Yuri reacts sooner.
If the players solve the case early, go to the finale. Do not invent more mystery.

entries.name: Finale Scaling — Level 3

entries.caption: Happy Orc Finale
rows: Yuri Kinnon; Ellie Felan; Grunt if available; 3 Hired Bandits.
Yuri Kinnon; Ellie Felan; Grunt if available; 4 Hired Bandits.

entries: If Grunt was neutralized earlier, remove him and do not replace him.

entries.name: Combat Audit
entries: Assume a full one-shot nova. Yuri is deliberately tougher than a Bandit Captain so he survives the opening burst.
Use enemy morale rather than hidden HP reductions to keep the ending moving. Hired muscle can surrender or flee once Yuri is down and the objective is lost.

entries.name: Difficulty Controls
entries: If the table is materially weaker than expected, have Ellie spend more turns on the evidence objective and movement instead of damage.
If the table is materially stronger than expected, use Grunt aggressively, keep the bandits coordinated, and make full use of Yuri's Dirty Fighting and reaction choice.

entries.name: One-Page Running Reference
entries: 4–5 level-3 PCs; three-hour target; three investigation beats.
Named cast only: Grog, Yuri, Sid, Grunt, Jim, Ellie.
Truth: Yuri is mastermind; Grunt burns stable; Jim lies that an orc fled; Ellie steals/plants evidence; Grog is innocent; Sid is ally.
Stable is not Grog's property.
Two independent Yuri links or one strong link plus decisive physical evidence is enough.
Finale: Happy Orc after evacuation. Yuri + Ellie + Grunt if available + 3 bandits (4 PCs) or 4 bandits (5 PCs).
Evidence is in the underground cellar reached from storage.
Use the embedded social and combat maps; replace the image's U-shaped bar with the real L-shaped bar at the table.

entries.name: Qualification-Test Reminders
entries: Ask quieter players directly what their characters are doing when one player dominates.
Restate known facts and ask for a decision if debate stalls.
Make a quick rules ruling and keep play moving when uncertain.
Reward clever methods by shortening the investigation rather than negating them.

trait.name: Cunning Action
entries: Yuri can take the Dash or Disengage action as a bonus action.

trait.name: Dirty Fighting (1/Turn)
entries: Yuri deals an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) damage on a weapon hit when he has advantage on the attack roll or an active ally is within 5 feet of the target.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Yuri makes three weapon attacks.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) piercing damage.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d4 + 4}) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: Yuri adds 3 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. He must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

reaction.name: Desperate Counterattack
entries: While Yuri has 47 hit points or fewer, when a creature within 5 feet misses him with an attack, Yuri can make one Shortsword attack against it. Yuri still has only one reaction per round.

trait.name: Spellcasting
entries: Ellie uses Intelligence for spellcasting (spell save DC 12, {@hit 4} to hit with spell attacks). She has the following spells prepared: at will: {@spell minor illusion}, {@spell ray of frost}; 1st level (4 slots): {@spell disguise self}, {@spell fog cloud}, {@spell magic missile}; 2nd level (2 slots): {@spell mirror image}, {@spell misty step}.

trait.name: Cunning Escape
entries: Ellie can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) piercing damage.

trait.name: Pack Muscle
entries: Grunt has advantage on a melee attack roll against a creature if at least one of Grunt's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Grunt makes two Mace attacks.

action.name: Mace
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Heavy Crossbow
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit 2} to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d10}) piercing damage.

action.name: Scimitar
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 3} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) slashing damage.

action.name: Light Crossbow
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit 3} to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d8 + 1}) piercing damage.
